Route calls to the correct regional base URL per connected account

approval.cost: No fee for API access is stated in the API docs; limits scale with the user's existing Jotform plan
approval.trigger: No review or approval of any kind is required before external users can connect. The official API docs describe no app submission, vetting, or listing process for API access, and no App Directory/marketplace listing for API integrations. There is no approval state at all; the operative limits are per-API-key daily call limits tied to the CONNECTED USER's Jotform plan (see Time).

blockers.detail: There is no documented scope system for API keys, so a connected key should be treated as broad access to that account. The JS SDK 'allow permissions' prompt does not translate into documented, enforceable permission subsets for the stored key.
blockers.howToClear: Treat stored keys as full-account credentials: encrypt at rest, minimize retention, and be transparent with users about the access level.
blockers.title: The credential you receive is the user's full API key, not a scoped token

blockers.detail: Because there is no OAuth, there is also no token refresh, no scoped consent, and no per-integration revocation handle exposed to you: your connection lives and dies with the user's key, which the user manages in their own account settings.
blockers.howToClear: Detect dead keys from API errors and route the user to re-issue/re-paste a key.
blockers.title: No revocation handle for the integrator

blockers.detail: A free/starter-plan user's key is capped at 1,000 calls/day regardless of your product's needs; heavy users must be on higher Jotform plans (or Enterprise) for the integration to scale. The docs also note: 'Jotform API v1 is mostly read only. You can get information about the Jotform user and forms. You can also download existing form data.'
blockers.howToClear: Check the connected user's plan tier at onboarding and set expectations for call volume.
blockers.title: Plan-dependent ceilings follow the end user, not you

alternatives: Manual key paste (the baseline variant of the same model: each user creates a key in My Account > API and pastes it into your product)
flavor.recommended: Per-user API key collection, via the JavaScript SDK login flow (JF.login + JF.getAPIKey) or manual key paste
flavor.why: There is no OAuth app object, and Jotform has no OAuth 2.0 program for third-party API access in its official API documentation: no client ID/client secret registration, no authorize/token endpoints, no redirect URI registration, no scope system. The connection object is a per-user API Key, created by each Jotform user in their own account (My Account > API section). The docs state the model plainly: 'To get started using Jotform API you need a valid API key', and the API 'is written for Jotform users and 3rd party developers who would like to serve Jotform users' (Zapier is given as the example). The closest thing to a consent flow is the JavaScript SDK: embed the SDK, call JF.login() to open a sign-in pop-up in an iframe; after sign-in the user 'will be asked to allow permissions to access to her account'; your code then calls JF.getAPIKey() to retrieve THAT USER's API key and stores it server-side ('you need to get the user's API key and save it in your servers'). What is handed over is the user's full API key, not a scoped, expiring token. Calls authenticate by API key as a query parameter (?apiKey=...), as an HTTP header (APIKEY: {myApiKey}), or via the SDK (JF.initialize({apiKey: ...})).

humanMust: (Each connecting user) Sign in to Jotform > My Account > API section > 'Create a new API Key' (only needed for the manual-paste flow; the JS SDK flow retrieves an existing key after sign-in)
name: Jotform
nuances: Region endpoints: the docs publish separate base URLs for standard (api.jotform.com), EU (eu-api.jotform.com), and HIPAA (hipaa-api.jotform.com) usage, so an integration must call the endpoint matching where the connected account's data resides rather than assuming one global host.

JS SDK flow constraints: JF.login() runs an iframe pop-up sign-in; after login the SDK auto-initializes with the key, and JF.getAPIKey() is how you persist access. This is a browser-mediated flow, so server-side/headless onboarding still falls back to manual key paste.

JSONP is supported (callback parameter), per the docs; relevant only to legacy browser integrations. Jotform's separate widgets/integrations platform (developers.jotform.com) also initializes with JF.connect({ apiKey: ... }), consistent with the key-based model; it is not an OAuth program.
prerequisites: Nothing to register: no developer account, portal enrollment, or credential issuance exists for the integrator
A secure server-side store for per-user API keys

steps.detail: There is no developer registration step. Build against the REST API at api.jotform.com (EU accounts: eu-api.jotform.com; HIPAA: hipaa-api.jotform.com).
steps.title: Build against the REST API

steps.detail: Option A (JS SDK): embed the SDK, call JF.login(); the user signs in in an iframe pop-up and allows permissions; call JF.getAPIKey() and save the returned key in your servers. Option B (manual): the user creates a key in My Account > API ('Create a new API Key') and pastes it into your product.
steps.time: ~30 min of code (SDK) or a settings paste
steps.title: Connect each user (SDK login or key paste)

steps.detail: Send the user's key on every call as the APIKEY header or ?apiKey= query parameter, against the regional base URL matching the account.
steps.title: Call the API with the stored key

tagline: There is no OAuth here at all: the connection is the user's own full-access API key, collected by paste or through Jotform's JS SDK login, and your call ceiling is whatever the connected user's Jotform plan allows per day.

time.active: ~30 min of integration code; no setup or registration
